scenario: [LNUL.4.1]: an interval relational operator propagates `null` ([LINT.4.5]). `lo` is `Int?`, so `(r.lo..r.hi)` is an interval with an absent endpoint. With `lo` absent, `(r.lo..r.hi) overlaps (0 .. 10)` and `(r.lo..r.hi) contains (3 .. 4)` are `null`, so neither `overlapping` nor `containing` fires, and no TypeError is raised: `saw_type_error` matches any `TypeError` fault fact ([LERR.9.3]) and must never fire. With `lo` 2 and `hi` 5 both relations hold and both rules fire, in source order ([LDET.5.4]). A runtime that read the absent endpoint as 0 would fire both on the first fact. PATH PINNED: the compiler's lowering of `overlaps` and `contains` into endpoint comparisons, each of which propagates `null`, evaluated by libds rete/eval.c and Mercury `ds.eval`.
rules_ds:
schema R scope logical:
    id: Int key
    lo: Int? mutable
    hi: Int mutable

rule overlapping:
    R r where (r.lo..r.hi) overlaps (0 .. 10)
->
    log info "overlaps"

rule containing:
    R r where (r.lo..r.hi) contains (3 .. 4)
->
    log info "contains"

rule saw_type_error:
    TypeError
->
    log critical "type error"
